description: The 6-stage sales call funnel for the Call Copilot stage tracker. Each stage gives the rep the goal, what to listen for, the verbatim lines to say, and when to advance. Sourced from MASTER-SALES-SCRIPT.md and sales-process/.

stages.name: 1. Introduction
stages.goal: Open with rapport, acknowledge the lead source + pain from triage, surface the outcome they want from this call, confirm the nudge they want to work with us, then future-pace into discovery.
stages.listen_for: Energy + tonality. The nudge — anything that says they want help / want to move forward. If they're flat or distracted, reposition before pushing on.
say: [Name], tell me about your day. (Open it up casual — let them set the tone.)

ACKNOWLEDGE: name where they came from (the lead source) and the pain they shared on the triage call. e.g. 'You came in from [source], and Mariana said the main thing for you right now is [pain] — does that still sound right?'
OUTCOME FRAME: So before we get into that — what do you want to have happen by the end of this meeting? What's an ideal outcome for you?
LISTEN FOR THE NUDGE: are they saying they want to work with us, or get help, or move forward? Tick 'Nudge confirmed' in the checklist above the moment you hear it.

FUTURE-PACE: Assuming you get all of that — assuming we figure out a way to make it happen — what happens next in your world? What does that unlock for you? (This surfaces the real desire and sets up discovery.)
stages.advance_when: They've named the outcome they want from the call AND you've ticked 'Nudge confirmed'. Then go straight to Discovery.

stages.name: 2. Discovery
stages.goal: Understand IF and HOW you can help. Cover the 7 beliefs (pain, doubt, cost, desire, money, support, trust). Eliminate objections before the close.
stages.listen_for: Discovery flags — vague answers, emotional words, numbers, spouse/team mentions, past attempts, hedging. The copilot will surface probes.
say: What's your biggest challenge right now? Or what's not working at the level it truly could be?
Tell me more — when you said [X], what do you mean exactly? Why do you say that though?
Tell me about the business — what do you sell, who's it for, and how long have you been running it? ... What part of running it drains you the most right now?
Take me back to the moment you realised the way you'd been growing this wasn't going to get you where you want — what was going on in the business that made you decide enough is enough?

CHUNK DOWN TO NUMBERS: Last week specifically, how many [leads / sales calls] did you generate? What about the week before? Out of those, how many fit the exact ideal client you want? ... Just for clarity — what was your exact revenue last month? What about the month before? (People tell stories about their problems; the truth is in the numbers.)
Assumption-correction: So you're making [guess] a month right now then, correct? (Make an assumption so they correct you with the truth.)

Begin with the end in mind — ultimately, where do you want the business to be? What's the revenue number you're driving toward, and what would the business look like at that point? Why that number specifically?
Can I ask another personal question — and I really hate to ask this — but what's your plan if nothing changes? What if the last five years are like the next five years?
I guess that makes sense — is there any other reason this is important to you now though?
Can I ask a personal question? The reason I'm asking is we want this to work around your lifestyle goals — what are the personal goals you want your business to allow you to achieve?

What else have you tried to fix this? What did you like or dislike about it? What we've found is when people don't get the result, it's one of two things — [blank] or [blank]. Which do you think it was?
Are you married? Is your partner supportive of the change? Do they know you're on this call — and what would they think if they knew?
stages.advance_when: You're 100% clear on their biggest challenge AND their real desire — business and personal. Not surface-level.

stages.name: 3. Transition
stages.goal: Move from questions to pitch with zero sales resistance — get the prospect to ask you to pitch them.
say: I don't think I have any more questions — is there anything else you feel like we haven't covered that you feel like I need to know?
Based on what you've told me, we can definitely help.

HAMBURGER TRANSITION: So where do you think we should go from here? I can walk you through exactly how we'd get you from [current] to [goal] if you want — but you tell me where you want to go. (Equal or downward inflection — never upward.)
stages.advance_when: They ask you to walk them through it.

stages.name: 4. Pitch
stages.goal: Sell the METHOD, not the deliverables. High-level promise -> 3 pillars -> delivery. Each pillar is the simultaneous explanation of why their past attempts failed and why this is different. Tie-down after every pillar.
stages.listen_for: Comprehension. If they say 'yeah' but clearly don't get it — stop and re-explain. Pillars 1 & 2 are paradigm shifts; 3 is the payoff.
say: PEN & PAPER: Do you have a pen and paper, something to take notes with, so I can break down those 3 things and how they'll get this working for you? (Pause until ready.)

FAVOUR FRAME: Now before I go over all the details, can I just ask you for a favour? ... Great — because we believe a healthy relationship begins with healthy communication. So while I may sound direct, it's because that'll allow you to get what you need to get [outcome] working. Is that fair enough? And on the other hand, I'll ask the same of you.

THREE WAYS: These calls go one of three ways. One, yes, it's amazing, I want to work with you guys. Two, no, it's not the right fit — and I want to let you know in advance it's totally okay if you say no to me, you won't hurt my feelings. But the third thing I want to stay away from is the maybe, the 'let me sleep on it', because a lot of the time that's just a polite way to say no. Does that sound fair enough?

PILLAR 1 — SELL THE VACATION (Messaging / Language): Have you been to Japan? ... So a while back I was on a trip in Japan, and I was super hungry — and I'll be honest with you, when I get hungry I do get a little hangry. So I was walking down the street with my family but I couldn't figure out what any of the restaurants were offering — even though they had tons of big, bold menus and signs outside — because Japanese is a language I don't understand. And it reminded me of this: the same thing is happening in your marketing right now. You could be spending tens of thousands more per month on ads, or posting content 10 times a day, but because your expertise isn't being communicated in a way your ideal client understands, it feels like you're speaking to them in a foreign language. So even if you put in more effort and time right now, it won't result in additional revenue. So — the first thing we're going to do for you is give you the right social media strategy, to make sure you're speaking in the right language, so your value is communicated in a way the right people understand and want. Are you following me so far?

PILLAR 1 DELIVERY: Great — and what's your schedule looking like over the next few days? ... Fantastic. So, should you decide to move forward on this call, I'll get Lauren to create your strategy for you — she'll look into your brand and tap into the psychology of your best possible client to identify the right platforms, content style and positioning for you. Then Mariana, who's run my socials for the last half-decade, will personally deliver it to you on a 1:1 call where you can ask her anything you'd like. Looking at her calendar, we can make [date] or [date] work — which suits you best? ... Fantastic. So what questions do you have about that part, specifically?

PILLAR 2 — CONTENT STRATEGY & SYSTEM: [Name], you seem pretty in shape — do you go to the gym, or what exercise do you do? ... So you know there are some people you see in the gym every time, always running on the treadmill, but they just don't seem to change body shape? They don't know what to do, what to eat outside the gym, so they get zero results — have you seen those people? ... Right. And there are also people who go to the gym only 3 times, stay just 30-40 minutes, and because they have a strategy on how to train and systems around what to eat, despite putting in less effort they're in amazing shape. That's the difference between just posting on social media, and posting with our AI Content System. It's how we get more than 100,000 views organically per week across our socials — but more importantly, how we drive revenue from social media. Do you see my posts a lot? ... Yep — someone who joined us last week, whose business was previously dependent on ads, booked 3 sales calls within 24 hours of starting with us. Because the AI Content System is based on all the data we've gathered from sharing 200,000+ of our own posts, and millions more on behalf of our clients. What used to take us 3 months and $25,000 to teach people, we can now hand to you at the click of a button. So we'll actually build this out FOR you — meaning you're left with an AI system that writes all your content for the week, specifically in your voice, so your accounts aren't just reaching more people, but your content results in real revenue. What do you feel that would do for your business? ... Does that make sense? What questions do you have about that specifically?

PILLAR 3 — SOCIAL MEDIA BRIDGE: Now imagine this. We're six weeks in the future and we've attracted all of your ideal clients here — and, can you see my hand? ... And you're over here on an island with the solution to what they want. No matter how big the traffic is, or how good your solution is — if there isn't a bridge connecting the two, they can't buy and work with you. There might be a couple of people who swim across, but you're losing out on the majority if you don't have a solid bridge. So that's why the last thing we'll do is give you the bridge — so you're left with prequalified prospects who are ready to buy.
stages.advance_when: You've covered all 3 pillars with a tie-down after each. Then run the conservative upside math and move to Committing.

stages.name: 5. Committing Phase
stages.goal: Get them 100% bought in on the thesis BEFORE money is on the table. Temp check -> onboarding -> price drop.
stages.listen_for: Tonality on the temp check. 'Dude, absolutely' = yes. 'I think so' = no.
say: What questions do you have about those [4] things specifically? (Answer in 1-2 sentences. Check for hidden objections: 'is there a specific reason you're asking?')

CONSERVATIVE UPSIDE MATH (before the temp check): Quick bit of math so this isn't abstract. You told me a client is worth about [LTV] to you. If this system just gets you one more client a month from organic — content you otherwise wouldn't even have posted — that's [LTV x 12] in extra revenue over the next 12 months. And that's the conservative version, just one more client a month.
How do you feel about the process specifically? Do you feel like that's what you need to get to [outcome]?

SCALE: What's really important to us is alignment — our team is all in. On a scale of 1-10, one being 'I hate this guy, get me off the phone,' ten being 'that's exactly what I need' — where do you fall exactly? ... What's keeping you from a 9 or 10? (Nothing in life is a 10 — it's not even 100% certain you'll wake up tomorrow. A 9 is about as close to certain as you'll ever be. And I'm not asking if you're a 10 on the price — in terms of the [4] things, do you feel in alignment?)
MINI-TRANSITION: So you feel really good about the process, no questions — what's next, where do you want to go from here? (Gets them to ask for the price.)

ONBOARDING (before price — removes the 'black hole' of the unknown so price lands against a clear picture): Basically, next steps — you'll process the investment with me. Once we take care of that, we set up an onboarding call, give you some homework, and lay out when we're going to meet, how often, what we'll give you and what we need from you — so you have complete clarity and certainty on exactly what's going to happen over the next 12 weeks. Does that sound good?
And the next steps are very simple — the investment is just [X]. (Soft, downward inflection, price ENDS the sentence on a period. Then go quiet — not a weird standoff.)
CLOSE: How do you feel? ... Cool, you sure? ... You ready to get started on some homework? ... What's your billing address?
stages.advance_when: After the price drop + close attempt, the prospect stalls or raises an objection. (If they say yes through the close, the sale is done — skip the Objections stage.)

stages.name: 6. Objections
stages.goal: Diffuse -> isolate -> handle uncertainty before logistics -> re-tie-down -> close. Loop until they're 100% in.
stages.listen_for: Which objection. The copilot detects it and surfaces the rebuttal. Handle UNCERTAINTY before money/support/timing.
say: THE UNIVERSAL HANDLE — run all 5 steps on EVERY objection before the specific rebuttal. Handle uncertainty before any logistic; a logistic handled while uncertainty is unresolved is a smoke screen.
STEP 1 — DIFFUSE: No problem. Not an issue at all. No problem. (Always, as a triple. Pause after it — it drops the pressure.)

STEP 2 — ISOLATE: Just so I can stay organized — when you say [objection], are you more in a 'should I do this' place where you're not 100% certain this is what you want, or a 'how can I do this' place where you're certain and it's just logistics? (Should I = uncertainty, handle the belief. How can I = logistic, trade and close.)
STEP 3 — TEMP CHECK: [Objection] aside — how do you feel about the process? Do you feel this is 100% what you need to get to [outcome], and that it's 100% going to work?

STEP 4 — SCALE (if they're still not certain): On a scale of 1 to 10 — one being 'get me off the phone', ten being 'that's exactly what I need' — where do you fall exactly? ... What's keeping you from a 9 or 10? (8 or under: 'why so low?' -> handle that -> re-ask the number. We don't do 7s.)
STEP 5 — DOUBLE TIE-DOWN: So [objection] aside — is there anything else keeping you from being less than 100% certain this is the right thing AND now is the right time? ... So you're 100% in?
SMOKESCREEN PROBE: if the tonality is off and the stated objection feels like a cover — For real, I can tell there's something. So what's really going on? What's really coming up for you?

THEN handle the specific objection — the copilot shows the verbatim rebuttal. Trade every concession for a decision AND a commitment: 'If I'm willing to do that for you, are you willing to move forward right now?'
stages.advance_when: They're 100% in and you've closed — move to Close Confirmation to button down the sale.

stages.name: 7. Close Confirmation
stages.goal: Button down the sale. Restate next steps, reassure, pre-frame against buyer's remorse, start onboarding momentum. The deal isn't safe until cash clears and onboarding begins.
stages.listen_for: Hesitation, second thoughts, a tone shift after the card is processed — post-close remorse. If it appears, handle it (see the buyers-remorse objection) — don't go silent.
say: Awesome — congratulations, this is a big move and I'm genuinely excited for you. Here's exactly what happens next: [restate the onboarding steps + first call date].

PRE-FRAME REMORSE: Real quick — right after a big decision like this, your brain might get loud and try to second-guess it. That's totally normal, it's the monkey brain doing its job. It doesn't mean it was the wrong call — it means it mattered. If anything comes up, you call me directly, okay?
Lock momentum: Let's get your onboarding form done right now while we're together, and get your first call on the calendar — momentum is what makes this work.
Reassure: You made a great decision. I've got your back — anytime you need anything, you reach out. Let's go get you [their outcome].
stages.advance_when: Payment has cleared, onboarding form is done, and the first call is booked. The sale is complete.
